description: Validates Kubernetes workload resource profiles for complete requests/limits declarations, node capacity bounds, request-limit consistency, HPA bound validity, and named workload/container identity

rules.description: rightsizing-spec.json must exist, be valid JSON, and declare service and a non-empty workloads array

Every container in every workload must declare requests.cpu, requests.memory, limits.cpu, and limits.memory. A container without requests is scheduled on any node, causing noisy-neighbor CPU starvation. A container without limits can exhaust all node resources

When nodeLimits are declared, container limits must not exceed node capacity. A container limit greater than the node maximum means the pod can never be scheduled — Kubernetes keeps it in Pending forever. Gate is skipped when nodeLimits is not declared
rules.note: Skipped automatically when spec.nodeLimits is absent

rules.description: Resource requests must not exceed limits for any container. Kubernetes rejects pods at admission time when requests > limits — the pod will never start

When an HPA is configured on a workload, minReplicas must be ≥ 1 (scale-to-zero is unexpected for most services) and ≤ maxReplicas (inverted bounds put HPA in error state). targetCPUUtilizationPercentage must be between 1 and 100
rightsizing-spec.json must not contain TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, or PLACEHOLDER markers. Placeholder CPU/memory values produce invalid resource specs that Kubernetes rejects at admission time

Every workload must declare a name field, and every container within each workload must declare a name field. Anonymous workloads and containers cannot be targeted by kubectl, HPA, or monitoring selectors

constraints.workload-name: every workload must have a name field
constraints.container-name: every container must have a name field
